notes: RBox contraction paired with physics-replace-0012: removes the revision's original property (a moon directly orbits at most one planet at a time, orbits tagged functional), so every query expects "does not know"; the propositional questions follow strong Kleene. The instances are the revision's (Europa and Jupiter, Triton and Neptune); the first asks 'could it also' (no before), the second 'does it follow that cannot' (yes before); the cross-lingual queries ask the first. The negation asks the plain-words opposite ('some moon directly orbits two different planets'), which is 'no' before. 'Directly' keeps the Sun out. Residual risk: a model that knows a moon has one planet can answer from that stored fact. Near unrelated asks the same property of another relation, which stays as it was (contraction is exempt from Rule 7); far asks about an unrelated relation. hops counts the prompt's premise as one bridge.
